sections.html:
Bellingham is a bayfront city of 96,395 people (July 1, 2025) and the seat of Whatcom County. You can list with an agent, sell on your own, or take a cash offer from a buyer who needs no mortgage. Western Washington University, Whatcom Community College and Bellingham Technical College keep rental and starter-home demand steady, and renters outnumber owners here, so many buyers are investors.

Housing measureBellingham figure
Owner-occupied housing rate, 2020 to 202444.6%

Buyers sort Bellingham by neighborhood before anything else. The city recognizes areas such as Alabama Hill, Barkley, Birchwood, Cordata, Cornwall Park, Edgemoor, Fairhaven, Happy Valley, the Lettered Streets, Roosevelt, Samish, Sehome, South Hill, Sunnyland, Whatcom Falls and York, along with the university district.

  • Fairhaven has a historic commercial district.
  • Sehome is part of today's downtown.
  • Cordata has a Whatcom Transportation Authority station near Bellis Fair Mall.
  • Alabama Hill is one of the higher points in town, at about 500 feet.

The Bellingham School District covers most of the city and runs four public high schools: Bellingham, Options, Sehome and Squalicum. A small northern slice lies in the Meridian School District, so verify the district for the exact address before you advertise.

Interstate 5 splits Bellingham and links it to Seattle and Vancouver. State Route 539 heads to Lynden and the border, and State Route 542 climbs toward Mount Baker. Whatcom Transportation Authority runs frequent Go Lines on several corridors, and Amtrak Cascades stops at Fairhaven Station twice a day.

Rainfall averages 34.84 inches a year, with November the wettest month. A winter pattern called a north-Easter can push Arctic air down the Fraser River Canyon with strong wind, and a warm Pineapple Express spell can melt snow fast enough to strain drainage. Inspectors and buyers look first at roofs, gutters, crawl spaces and drainage.

Lake Whatcom supplies the city's drinking water and forms part of its eastern edge, which is why short-term rentals are barred inside the watershed.

Bellingham runs a Rental Registration and Safety Inspection Program under Bellingham Municipal Code 6.15. Owners register each rental, pass a safety inspection before renting, renew the rental license every year, and have the property re-inspected about every three to three and a half years. The program now requires a city checklist for private inspectors and offers a single appeal step. Tenants get 120 days of notice before a rent increase, and an increase of 8 percent or more triggers relocation assistance under BMC 6.14.

  • Short-term rentals fall under BMC 20.10.037 and need a land use permit.
  • In residential zones the operator must live there at least 270 days a year, and the whole home can be rented no more than 95 days a year.
  • Short-term rentals are not allowed in the Lake Whatcom watershed or in shoreline areas.
  • Detached accessory dwelling units cannot be short-term rentals in single-family zones.

Inherited a rented Bellingham house? Call the Permit Center at 360-778-8300 and ask for the registration and inspection record before you list.

The seller owes real estate excise tax in Washington, and the state portion is graduated under RCW 82.45.060. For sales starting January 1, 2027, the bands are 1.1 percent up to $551,000, 1.28 percent up to $1,551,000, 2.75 percent up to $3,051,000 and 3 percent above. The local rate is added, and the county treasurer works that out for the parcel.

  • RCW 82.45.080 makes the tax the seller's obligation, due at the time of sale.
  • Interest starts after one month, and penalties of 5, 10 and 20 percent apply at one, two and three months under RCW 82.45.100.
  • A Real Estate Excise Tax Affidavit must reach the Whatcom County Treasurer, on the first floor of the courthouse at 360-778-5160, before the Auditor will record the deed.
  • The deed's first page needs a three inch top margin, grantor and grantee names, a legal description and the 16 digit assessor parcel number.

You also owe the buyer a completed disclosure statement on improved residential property. It is due five business days after both sides sign, unless the buyer waives it or an exemption applies, and the buyer then has three business days to rescind (RCW 64.06.020).

Statements go out in mid-February. Half is due April 30 and the remainder October 31, and a bill under $50 is due in full on April 30. A date that lands on a weekend or holiday moves to the next business day. Skipping the first half turns the whole year delinquent, with interest and penalty figured on the full year at the rates in RCW 84.56.020.

If the sale closes in spring or fall, ask the closing agent how the current half will be divided between you and the buyer. A missing statement does not stop interest, so look up the bill online even when nothing arrives by mail.

sections.h2: Your options for a quick sale
sections.html:
Three routes cover most Bellingham sellers, and the right one depends on the condition of the house, the tenants and your closing date.

  • List with an agent and prepare for showings, which suits a clean, vacant property in a sought-after neighborhood.
  • Sell it yourself, which saves the commission but leaves marketing, disclosure forms and negotiation to you.
  • Take a cash offer, which fits a house that needs work, a rental with an inspection problem, an inherited property or a tight deadline.

On any route, collect the last property tax statement, rental registration paperwork, utility account details and the recorded deed. Compare a cash offer with what a listing would net after commission, repairs and carrying costs.

sections.h2: What happens after you accept an offer
sections.html: Escrow opens, and title work finds any unpaid taxes or liens. You sign the excise tax affidavit and the deed, and the treasurer collects the tax before the deed is recorded. Sellers of a rental should confirm the city registration is current, since buyers often ask. A cash buyer without a lender skips the appraisal and loan approval, so the closing date usually depends on title work and how soon your documents are ready.

faqs.q: Can I sell my Bellingham house as-is?
faqs.a: Yes, and many owners do. Washington still expects a completed seller disclosure statement on improved residential property unless the buyer waives it or the transfer is exempt, so list known defects honestly.

faqs.q: Who pays real estate excise tax when a Bellingham house sells?
faqs.a: The seller does, under RCW 82.45.080. The state portion is graduated from 1.1 percent, and the county treasurer adds the local rate when the affidavit is filed.

faqs.q: When are Whatcom County property taxes due?
faqs.a: April 30 for the first half and October 31 for the second half. Bills under $50 are due in full on April 30, and a weekend or holiday due date moves to the next business day.

faqs.q: Do I need to deal with the rental program if my Bellingham house was a rental?
faqs.a: Yes. While the house is rented, the owner keeps the city registration current and renews it every year. Ask the Permit Center at 360-778-8300 about the registration and the last safety inspection before you sell.

faqs.q: Can a buyer use my Bellingham house as a short-term rental?
faqs.a: Only with a city permit and within zoning limits. Residential zones require the operator to live there at least 270 days a year, whole-home rental is capped at 95 days a year, and the Lake Whatcom watershed and shoreline areas are closed.
